long_context_same_items.policy: Reported baseline: uniform 100,000-token cap for all 106 items, same proportional per-class truncation. Items whose prompt is under the cap send exactly the prompt of the earlier run and were served from the cache (identical prompt, no new call). Answered: 102/106; unscored: 4 (4%). Truncated at this cap: 33 of the scored items. Unscored items remain, so long-context is reported ONLY on the scored items, with the size distribution of scored vs unscored, and every system is compared on exactly those items (no further cap change, no model switch).

The verifier turned judgements into `unsure` (an abstention): final agentic has 86 `unsure` judgements against 1 for class-aware. No threshold or rule was changed.

verifier_diagnostics.label: post hoc diagnostic; does not replace the frozen verifier

t3_setup: 60 (paragraph, as-of date) items from 20 Directions, 30 before and 30 after the effective date, gold {'in_force_original': 30, 'amended': 21, 'deleted': 9}. Parser: 196 parsed actions from 988 amendment instructions (rules v2). Parse precision on Karan's 20-row spot-check: rules v1 15/20 (Wilson 0.53–0.89); after one rule fix (merged within-paragraph changes, per-item exception dates, 'dated' references ignored), the same 20 rows: 20/20 (Wilson 0.84–1.00), assessed against Karan's notes, not re-checked by a human. The target paragraph is pinned into the evidence (a deleted one stays, marked); the verifier does not apply to a status answer.
t3_precision: Post-fix, same rows the fix was designed on (in-sample): 20/20. This is Claude's reading of Karan's notes on the rows that motivated the fix, not an independent measurement.

Independent post-fix check (10 seeded parses behind frozen items, none among the first 20): 8/10, Wilson 95% [0.49, 0.94]; 8 dependent items dropped (T3-005, T3-006, T3-015, T3-016, T3-051, T3-052, T3-059, T3-060) and T3 recomputed on the remaining 52. Display note: both parses marked wrong are 'adoption or 1 April 2026, whichever is earlier' amendments. The parser stores them as a window [publication date, 1 April 2026] (status unknown inside it); the sheet printed that as 'window: 2025-12-04 to 2026-04-01 (whichever earlier)', which the rater read as a claimed effective date of 4 December 2025. The dropped items' as-of dates lie outside the window (before publication / after 1 April 2026), so their gold would be the same under either reading; the human labels stand as recorded and the drop is kept (conservative).
Of the 60 frozen items, 6 come from the 20 checked parses (3 parses: T3-003, T3-004, T3-025, T3-026, T3-057, T3-058); the other 54 rest on parses not in the first check.

14 items come from multi-change instructions affected by the known 'old words' defect (a merged change's recorded old words also include the previous change's new words; it can only exclude candidates as corpus-version 'unclear', never change an included item's gold): T3-017, T3-018, T3-019, T3-020, T3-025, T3-026, T3-027, T3-028, T3-035, T3-036, T3-045, T3-046, T3-057, T3-058.

limitations: API outage: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` returned HTTP 503 'high demand' to every call from 2026-09-28 20:09:51 IST until the first successful probe at 2026-09-28 22:19:25 IST; intermittent 503s continued during the runs, the last at 2026-09-29 01:59:44 IST (5 of 12 probes unavailable). The long-context runs paused and resumed around them; no model switch was made.
The P4 LLM is a free Flash-Lite-class model (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`); P3-002's genuine answers used Groq `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. These results describe this model, not frontier models.
The prompt cache is shared between paired systems (see Shared prompts): at temperature 0 this is identical to re-calling.
Long-context: 102 items (not the full 106; compare on the same items only); truncation to the cap is proportional per class and counted per item; call failures are listed, never scored.
T3 circularity: the gold and the temporal filter come from the same parser; T3 measures whether the LLM uses the dates.

Temporal: the corpus holds only the current (amended) text of each Direction. The system can flag that a paragraph was amended later ('original in force; amended from <date>'), but it cannot show the pre-amendment wording, so for an as-of date before an amendment it may state the post-amendment rule (see the date-specific demo transcript).
T3 parse precision after the rule fix is Claude's reading of Karan's notes on the same 20 rows, not a new human check.

The T1 verifier (whole cited paragraph as NLI premise, fixed rule) abstains on about a fifth of items and does not raise precision on the items it keeps (post hoc diagnostic a); a single-sentence premise would not raise support (diagnostic b).
T3 parse precision: only 6 of the 60 frozen items rest on parses in the first human check; the independent check covers 10 more parses (24 items).
The T4 unsupported-sentence rate is an NLI proxy, and the verifier and RePASs share an NLI model.
n per task: T1 106 items (long-context 102); T2 t2_xclass_t1 291, t2_xclass_p2002 53, t2_supp_p2003 25; T3 52; T4 28 primary (30 shown). One human rater for every human label.
The class-aware gain is for retrieving/judging against the named target class; it is not a general class-blind vs class-aware verdict (P3-001).

The P3-002 gameability verdict uses its pre-registered rule (reproduces iff the CI lies at or above 0). P4 labels use 'excludes 0' only when the CI is strictly above or below 0. No reported P3-002 result lies on the boundary, so the two conventions never disagree here (checked: none of the 12 P3-002 verdict CIs, 6 gameability and 6 repair ranking, main and sensitivity, has a bound at 0).

deviations.text: The T1 rationale instruction was reworded after format debugging on 5 rejected (non-gold) items, before the prompt freeze: the model wrote 'The matched paragraph …' meta-sentences that nothing can entail.
The client-side throttle estimates tokens as characters / 3 (was / 4) after a per-minute input-token 429 on ~150K-token prompts. The 12 RPM / 200K TPM limits are unchanged.
A call that keeps failing is recorded as a call failure (not written, not scored, never counted as an abstention) and retried on the next run.

deviations.kind: deviation (one rule fix, as the prompt allows)
deviations.text: T3 parser rules v2 after the spot-check (15/20): merged within-paragraph changes, per-item exception dates, 'dated <date>' references ignored. Known defect frozen with the set: merged changes' old words include the previous change's new words.

T3 precision: v1 15/20 reported as the human figure; 20/20 only as in-sample post-fix; an independent 10-parse check (spot-check 2) on parses behind frozen items; items from the checked parses and from defect-affected instructions listed.

Long-context calls: at most 3 attempts per item per run with exponential backoff and jitter, every attempt in the ledger; network drops and read timeouts retried as transient; a 300 s read timeout for these prompts; after the remainder run and one full retry pass, > 20% of the 30-item subset still failing triggers a rerun of the whole baseline at one uniform 100K cap. Prompt-token distributions of scored vs failed items are reported and every system is compared on exactly the scored items.

Verifier diagnostics without LLM calls: precision on non-abstained items, and support under a best-single-sentence premise with the count of premises over 512 tokens. Diagnostic only; the frozen verifier is unchanged.
The P3-001 framing paragraph sits directly above the T2 class-filter results, with hybrid_minus_source_class next to them.

The note-2 fallback was triggered EARLY: the long-context baseline is rerun on all 106 items at one uniform 100K cap (same proportional per-class truncation) without first finishing the 150K remainder run and retry pass. The decision was based ONLY on the failure-size evidence: never-answered prompts had a median of about 150K tokens (14 items, range 60K–150K) against about 71K for the 47 scored items (range 6K–132K). Disclosure: long-context scores on those 47 scored items had already been computed and displayed in Claude's session (3-way flag F1 0.515 [0.374, 0.626] against final agentic 0.518 on the same items) before Claude recommended the rerun; Claude's recommendation cited only the size evidence, and Karan decided on that evidence. The 150K run's items are kept only as a record, never reported as the baseline. Items under 100K reuse the cache (identical prompt). Pre-committed next step: if more than 20% of items still fail at 100K after one retry pass, one step down to a uniform 64K cap for all items; if failures remain after that, long-context is reported only on the scored items with the size distribution and every system compared on exactly those items; no further cap changes. A health probe and a 3-consecutive-failure circuit breaker stop provider outages from spending quota.

Before the outage cutoff, the 37 long-context items whose 100K prompt is byte-identical to a cached 150K prompt were scored from the cache (cache-only mode: no API call, no ledger entry); their outputs are identical to the 150K run. Gemini then recovered overnight and the chain completed the 100K pass and one retry pass: 102 of 106 items answered, 4 still failing (4%, below the 20% step-down threshold, so no 64K rerun). The demo transcripts ran on Gemini; the Groq demo fallback was never used.

Claude stopped the 150K remainder step on the 3-hour compute rule using wall-clock time (4 h). Measured as actual run time (Mac awake, from the power log), that step ran about 62 minutes (6 + 55 min), so the rule was not reached. Run times in this report are active time (macOS monotonic clock, which stops while the Mac sleeps); wall time is shown alongside.

The Part A statement that a windowed NLI premise would support far more rationales (15/27 vs 25/27, 5 debug items, 3-sentence window) does not hold on the validation outputs: a best-single-sentence premise supports fewer (see diagnostic b).

summary: The class filter improves T2 retrieval: nDCG@10 ON − OFF t2_xclass_t1 +0.451 [+0.421, +0.481] (excludes 0 (above)), t2_xclass_p2002 +0.423 [+0.336, +0.514] (excludes 0 (above)), t2_supp_p2003 +0.171 [+0.072, +0.273] (excludes 0 (above)). The gain is partly built in: relevance was labelled only for the target-class counterpart.

The class filter shows no significant effect on T1 judgement: 3-way flag F1 -0.049 [-0.133, +0.036] (does not exclude 0) with the verifier on, -0.050 [-0.133, +0.027] (does not exclude 0) without it (n = 106).
The verifier lowers T1 3-way flag F1 by -0.068 [-0.132, -0.012] (excludes 0 (below)) and coverage by -0.217 [-0.292, -0.142] (excludes 0 (below)) (n = 106).

No LLM system significantly beats the P2-002 candidate labels on collapsed F1 (the fair comparison): Class-blind LLM − P2-002 -0.019 [-0.114, +0.072] (does not exclude 0); Class-aware LLM − P2-002 +0.024 [-0.096, +0.135] (does not exclude 0); Final agentic − P2-002 -0.074 [-0.192, +0.036] (does not exclude 0); Class-blind + verifier − P2-002 -0.089 [-0.186, +0.006] (does not exclude 0).
The class-blind LLM has the highest 3-way flag F1 (0.602).

Every LLM system is weak on 'different' judgements (F1 class-blind LLM 0.321 / class-aware LLM 0.154 / final agentic 0.047 / class-blind + verifier 0.176), so class-specific differences are the benchmark's hardest case.

Long-context (100K cap, n = 102) is statistically tied with P2-002, class-blind and class-aware on both flag metrics (paired CIs: P2-002 3-way +0.057 [-0.044, +0.163] (does not exclude 0), collapsed +0.045 [-0.093, +0.176] (does not exclude 0); class-blind 3-way -0.097 [-0.197, +0.010] (does not exclude 0), collapsed +0.054 [-0.047, +0.159] (does not exclude 0); class-aware 3-way -0.035 [-0.128, +0.063] (does not exclude 0), collapsed +0.023 [-0.088, +0.142] (does not exclude 0)), matches final agentic on 3-way F1 (+0.030 [-0.067, +0.129] (does not exclude 0)), and beats final agentic (+0.126 [+0.016, +0.240] (excludes 0 (above))) and class-blind + verifier (+0.127 [+0.018, +0.234] (excludes 0 (above))) on collapsed F1. It is as weak as the other LLM systems on 'different' judgements (F1 0.074).
